# Areas

## Purpose

Aspects of life and work that require ongoing attention and a maintained standard of quality. An area answers the question “What am I responsible for, and what do I maintain?” It has no single completion date.

## Include

- Ongoing responsibilities, recurring procedures, rules, and personal standards.
- Current information needed to manage a particular aspect of life or work.
- Periodic reviews of an area's condition and records of recurring activities.
- Examples: “Health” with medical checkup records and habits, “Personal finances” with a budget and recurring payments, “Home” with property maintenance, and “Work” with ongoing duties.

## Exclude

- Tasks with a distinct final outcome, even within this area — the Projects folder (`1 Projects`). For example, “Health” is an area, while “Prepare for a half marathon” is a project.
- Articles and reference materials on a topic without an ongoing responsibility — the Resources folder (`3 Resources`).
- Responsibilities that are no longer current and materials from discontinued areas — the Archives folder (`4 Archives`).

## Placement guidelines

Create a separate subfolder for each area when helpful. Its description should state the responsibility, the standard to maintain, and recurring activities.

The deciding criterion is an ongoing practical responsibility. Interest in a topic alone belongs in resources. Projects associated with an area stay in the Projects folder and can be connected to the area through links.
